title: Old English Poetic Meter
subtitle: Alliterative verse — four stresses, caesura, no end-rhyme.
objectives: Read and translate authentic Old English poetry and prose.

sections.heading: Content
sections.body: Old English poetry is alliterative. Each line has four primary stresses divided by a caesura (mid-line pause). The first three stresses alliterate; the fourth does not. Alliteration is on the first sound of the stressed syllable. Vowels alliterate with any vowel. No end-rhyme. Example from Beowulf: 'Hwæt! Wē Gār-Dena / in gēardagum' — three g-sounds alliterate (Gār, gēardagum) across the caesura.
